question: What isolation properties must camera and `browser.proxy` provide beyond the current capability allowlists, Windows camera consent, loopback binding, and bearer authentication?
rationale: This determines whether the existing paths should be formally accepted or replaced by MXC or dedicated brokers, with material security, compatibility, and user-consent tradeoffs.

options.title: Per-tool least privilege
options.body: Specify separate camera and browser invariants and introduce brokers or sandboxing only where the current controls fail them.

options.title: MXC-first boundary
options.body: Require both tool families to execute through MXC and accept the associated Windows API and browser integration work.

options.title: Formalize current model
options.body: Accept the current in-process capture and authenticated proxy architecture after threat review, then document and test its guarantees.

recommendation.title: Per-tool least privilege
recommendation.body: Specify separate camera and browser invariants and introduce brokers or sandboxing only where the current controls fail them.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the camera path, raised the issue to P1, and has recent adjacent sandbox history; the MXC contributors are strong technical reviewers.
